- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not continue falling beyond 1–2% below recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply 1–2% downward adjustment to first 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.33–0.67), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before projecting.
